The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate and initialize data structures\n    std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);                 // Dense vector\n    std::vector<double> h_out(numRows);                 // Output vector\n\n i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n    printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n    printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n           nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n    printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate and initialize data structures\n    std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);                 // Dense vector\n    std::vector<double> h_out(numRows);                 // Output vector\n\n    printf(\"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n    fill(h_vec.data(), numRows, maxVal);\n    fill(h_val.data(), nItems, maxVal);\n    initRandomMatrix(h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), nItems, numRows);\n\n    // For validation, compute reference solution\n    std::vector<double> h_reference;\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Computing reference solution...\\n\");\n        h_reference.resize(numRows);\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), \n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_reference.data());\n    }\n\n    // Perform SpMV computation\n    printf(\"Computing SpMV...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (index_t iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_out.data());\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    const double avgTime = duration.count() / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n    \n    printf(\"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(h_out, \"OutputVector\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        const bool valid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), numRows);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\nCuda compilation tools, release 12.0, V12.0.140\nBuild cuda_12.0.r12.0/compiler.32267302_0\ncmake version 3.30.2\n\nCMake suite maintained and supported by Kitware (kitware.com/cmake).","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

    number of rows/columns in the matrix\\n//\\n// ****************************************************************************\\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const i < 34; ++i) init[i] = init[i - 31];\n        for (int i = 34; i < 64; ++i) init[i] = init[i - 31] + init[i - 3];\n\n        // We need r[t-31 .. t-1] with t = outputIndex + 344. Parallelized with OpenMP via jump-ahead.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fillRange(double* A, const uint64_t skip, const uint64_t count, const double maxVal) {\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const uint64_t nt = omp_get_num_threads();\n        const uint64_t t = omp_get_thread_num();\n        const uint64_t b = count * t / nt;\n        const uint64_t e = count * (t + 1) / nt;\n        if (b < e) {\n            GlibcRand rng(1, skip + b);\n            for (uint64_t i = b; i < e; ++i) {\n                A[i] = maxVal * (rng.next() / (static_cast<double>(GLIBC_RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrixLocal\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Builds rows [rowBegin, rowEnd) of the CSR matrix that the original\n//   serial initRandomMatrix() generates (identical result).                                                            \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                 \\\n        }                                                                                 \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Class: GlibcRand\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Bit-exact reimplementation of glibc's rand() (TYPE_3 additive feedback\n//   generator, r[i] = r[i-31] + r[i-3]) with O(log n) jump-ahead, so that\n//   independent threads/ranks can produce any slice of the sequence that\n//   the original serial code obtains from srand()/rand().\n//\n//   Output number k (0-based) after srand(seed) equals r[k + 344] >> 1.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nclass GlibcRand {\n  public:\n    GlibcRand(uint32_t seed, uint64_t outputIndex) {\n        uint32_t init[64];\n        int32_t word = static_cast<int32_t>(seed == 0 ? 1 : seed);\n        init[0] = static_cast<uint32_t>(word);\n        for (int i = 1; i < 31; ++i) {\n            const int32_t hi = word / 127773;\n            const int32_t lo = word % 127773;\n            word = 16807 * lo - 2836 * hi;\n            if (word < 0) word += 2147483647;\n            init[i] = static_cast<uint32_t>(word);\n        }\n        for (int i = 31; i < 34; ++i) init[i] = init[i - 31];\n        for (int i = 34; i < 64; ++i) init[i] = init[i - 31] + init[i - 3];\n\n        // We need r[t-31 .. t-1] with t = outputIndex + 344. Since the\n        // recurrence r[s+31] = r[s+28] + r[s] holds for s >= 3, use the\n        // polynomial x^k mod (x^31 - x^28 - 1) with base r[3..33].\n        const uint64_t k = outputIndex + 344 - 34;\n        uint32_t c[31];\n        polyPowX(k, c);\n        for (int m = 0; m < 31; ++m) {\n            uint32_t s = 0;\n            for (int j = 0; j < 31; ++j) s += c[j] * init[3 + m + j];\n            buf_[m] = s;  // r[t-31+m]\n            if (m < 30) mulX(c);\n        }\n        pos_ = 31;\n    }\n\n    // Returns the next value exactly as glibc rand() would.\n    inline uint32_t next() {\n        // buffer index i&31 holds r[i]; r[i-31] at (i+1)&31, r[i-3] at (i-3)&31\n        const uint32_t v = buf_[(pos_ + 1) & 31] + buf_[(pos_ - 3) & 31];\n        buf_[pos_ & 31] = v;\n        ++pos_;\n        return v >> 1;\n    }\n\n  private:\n    uint32_t buf_[32];\n    uint32_t pos_;\n\n    // c(x) <- c(x) * x mod P(x)\n    static void mulX(uint32_t* c) {\n        const uint32_t top = c[30];\n        for (int j = 30; j > 0; --j) c[j] = c[j - 1];\n        c[0] = top;\n        c[28] += top;\n    }\n\n    static void polyMulMod(const uint32_t* a, const uint32_t* b, uint32_t* out) {\n        uint32_t p[61] = {0};\n        for (int i = 0; i < 31; ++i) {\n            if (a[i] == 0) continue;\n            for (int j = 0; j < 31; ++j) p[i + j] += a[i] * b[j];\n        }\n        for (int d = 60; d >= 31; --d) {\n            p[d - 3] += p[d];\n            p[d - 31] += p[d];\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; Parallelized with OpenMP via jump-ahead.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fillRange(double* A, const uint64_t skip, const uint64_t count, const double maxVal) {\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const uint64_t nt = omp_get_num_threads();\n        const uint64_t t = omp_get_thread_num();\n        const uint64_t b = count * t / nt;\n        const uint64_t e = count * (t + 1) / nt;\n        if (b < e) {\n            GlibcRand rng(1, skip + b);\n            for (uint64_t i = b; i < e; ++i) {\n                A[i] = maxVal * (rng.next() / (static_cast<double>(GLIBC_RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrixLocal\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Builds rows [rowBegin, rowEnd) of the CSR matrix that the original\n//   serial initRandomMatrix() generates (identical result). ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrixLocal(std::vector<index_t>& cols, std::vector<uint64_t>& rowPtr,\n                           const        if (static_cast<double>(GLIBC_RAND_MAX) / GLIBC_RAND_MAX <= prob) {\n            lo = GLIBC_RAND_MAX;\n        } else {\n            while (hi - lo > 1) {\n                const int64_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;\n                if (static_cast<double>(mid) / GLIBC_RAND_MAX <= prob) lo = mid; else hi = mid;\n            }\n        }\n        thr = lo;\n    }\n    const uint32_t thrU = 1, 0);\n    const int maxThreads = omp_get_max_threads();\n    std::vector<std::vector<index_t>> threadCols(maxThreads);\n    std::vector<index_t> threadRowBegin(maxThreads + 1, localRows);\n\n#pragma      if (t == nt - 1) threadRowBegin[nt] = localRows;\n        auto& my = threadCols[t];\n        my.reserve(static_cast<size_t>((re - rb) * (static_cast<double>(dim) * prob * 1.05 + 16)));\n        if (rb < re) {\n            GlibcRand rng(seed, static_cast<uint64_t>(rowBegin + rb) * dim);\n            for (index_t r = rb; r < re; ++r) {\n                const size_t before = my.size();\n rowPtr[r]);\n        index_t p = 0;\n        bool dirty = false;\n        const uint64_t hb = rowPtr[r], he = rowPtr[r + 1];\n        for (uint64_t h = hb; h <= he && !dirty; ++h) {\n            // segment [p, q]; q is the next hit column (check happens before the decision)\n            const bool isHit = h < he;\n            const index_t q = isHit ? cols[h] : dim - 1;\n            if (!isHit ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const uint64_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvSellKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   GPU SpMV on a SELL-32 layout: one thread per row, element k of the ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(BLOCK_SIZE)\nspmvSellKernel(const index_t rows, const uint64_t* __restrict__ double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t r = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (r >= rows) return;\n    const index_t* c = cols + sliceOffsets[r >> SLICE_SHIFT] + (r & (SLICE - 1));\n    const double* v = val + sliceOffsets[r >> SLICE_SHIFT] + (r & (SLICE - 1));\n    const index_t len = rowLen[r];\n    double t = 0.0;\n    index_t k = 0;\n    for (; k + 4 <= len; k += 4) {\n SLICE), v2 = __ldcs(v + 2 * SLICE),\n                     v3 = __ldcs(v + 3 * SLICE);\n        const double x0 = __ldg(vec + c0), x1 = __ldg(vec + c1), x2 = __ldg(vec + c2),\n                     x3 = ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n    printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n    printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n           nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n    printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate and initialize data structures\n    std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows); {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfetBbLUairUSCXFdD8mU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've rewritten `spmv/spmv.cpp` and `spmv/CMakeLists.txt` to use MPI, OpenMP and CUDA together; it's always hybrid, with no fallback path. The executable is still `spmv` and there are no new files or external dependencies.\n\n**Correctness:** the output is bit-for-bit identical to the original. The output hash from `-r` matches the original program for every size, sparsity and value setting I tried, including tiny matrices, fully dense ones (`-s 1`), and runs with more MPI processes than rows, on 1 to 6 processes. Validation (`-v`) passes in all of them.\n\n**Performance** (40000×40000 matrix, 160M nonzeros, RTX 3090s):\n\n| | Time per iteration | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original (1 CPU core) | ~250 ms | 1.3 |\n| 1 process / 1 GPU | 2.23 ms | 143 |\n| 2 processes / 2 GPUs | 1.13 ms | 283 |\n| 4 processes / 4 GPUs | 0.64 ms | ~500 |\n\nOne GPU reaches about 90% of the card's memory-bandwidth limit. Matrix setup is parallel too: it took 31 s in the original and about 1–2 s now.\n\n**How the work is split:**\n- **MPI:** each process takes an equal block of rows and uses one GPU (assigned by its rank within the node). Each process generates only its own rows, so memory per process shrinks as you add processes. The result is gathered onto process 0 for printing and validation.\n- **OpenMP (matrix setup):** the original builds the matrix with billions of serial `rand()` calls. I reimplemented glibc's `rand()` exactly, with the ability to jump to any position in its sequence. Every thread can start partway through the sequence and still produce the original matrix. The original's end-of-matrix rules (\"stop at the nonzero limit\" / \"fill the remaining entries\") are detected exactly; the affected rows, usually only the last few, are then regenerated serially.\n- **CUDA:** one GPU thread per row, with the matrix stored so neighbouring threads read neighbouring memory. Each row is still summed in the original order with separate multiply and add steps (no fused multiply-add), because the original binary uses none. That is why the output is identical.\n- **OpenMP (main loop):** the original generator can create a few very long rows at the end of the matrix (20,894 entries against an average of 4,000 here). Summing those one after another on the GPU was the bottleneck, so the CPU computes them each iteration while the GPU handles everything else.\n\n**Timing:** the timed section now also includes waiting for the GPU and gathering the result onto process 0, so the number covers having the full answer on the host.\n\n**Launching:** Open MPI pins each process to a single core by default when you run 1 or 2 processes, which leaves OpenMP with one thread. That only slows setup: wall time went from about 7 s to 11.6 s in my 1-process run, and the timed loop is unaffected. Launch with `mpirun --bind-to none` or `--map-by ...:PE=<cores>`, and run one process per GPU."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":201,"cache_read_input_tokens":100444,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":201},"output_tokens":764,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0866fb50-b614-4cae-9163-96fb88c8bb75","uuid":"1df2161a-75c3-4181-867e-194dffef64df","timestamp":"2026-10-03T07:08:46.985Z","request_id":"req_011CfetBb27mJusiUFmUkghb"}
